messages.body_plain:
Hello,

As I have been testing the RStudio 0.99.1285, I have noticed a few things with Packrat that I'm not quite sure if they should be happenning or not. In my project, I currently have two Packrat libraries, which probably should not be happening. It could be because I have upgraded my R version from 3.3.0 to 3.3.1, and I think Packrat has maybe attempted to load both the folders with the lock file.

I've also noticed some issues with trying to remove packages from my library, and I can't seem to figure out why I can't remove a package from my session..

Lastly, I've installed a package from CRAN, but in Packrat it does not show where it comes from, nor can I reinstall or remove it from my session. Thoughts on how to proceed moving forward?
I have attached my session info, as I'm not really sure where to start with diagnosing these issues, as well as the packrat lock file.

Thank you Kevin for all the hard work you have put into Packrat. Not trying to bash on it, but just to give some feedback on some issues I have experienced.

messages.subject: Re: Two Packrat Libraries in one RStudio Project?
messages.subject_clean: Two Packrat Libraries in one RStudio Project?
messages.body_plain:
Interesting; thanks. It looks like the libraries as set by packrat are what we would expect, so I'm curious why RStudio is reporting something inconsistent with the current library paths.

Does explicitly refreshing the packages pane help? There should be a little refresh icon near the top-right of the packages pane that you can click to refresh the package listing.

It's also possible that (as you said) the package 'brew' is showing up in the packages pane as it's detected as a dependency of a currently installed package, even though it itself is not currently installed. If you execute 'packrat::status()', does it report something to that effect? (The package 'brew' is required by your project but is not installed, or something to that effect)

All I've found so far is the example at richfitz/wood <https://github.com/richfitz/wood/>, but that looks more complex than what I think I need. I've also asked this on SO just now: http://stackoverflow.com/q/39009579/1036500

> Can someone point me towards a working example where packrat <https://rstudio.github.io/packrat/> is used with AppVeyor <https://ci.appveyor.com/> or Travis-CI to build an R package? Searching through Google and GitHub, I can't find any packrat-enable package that uses AppVeyor.  For Travis, I've found a few examples <https://github.com/richfitz/wood/blob/master/.travis.yml> that use @craig-citro 's initial r-travis <https://github.com/craigcitro/r-travis> approach, but I'd like to start this package with the newer approach of native R support <http://docs.travis-ci.com/user/languages/r/>.
>
> Do the yaml files need to change? Are there some settings I need to add through the Travis/AppVeyor websites?  I have a very minimal package (testthat is the only dependency) that broke Travis & AppVeyor builds. Here is the code frozen for that commit <https://github.com/OuhscBbmc/Premiss/tree/f110944be3e1b02d53ffbe69b71fc5d2d9dd6615>. The following is a test to show the difference

This is what it looks like on a network drive (H:/):

> packrat::init(restart = FALSE)

Initializing packrat project in directory:

- "H:/git/testProj/testProj"

Packrat mode off. Resetting library paths to:

- "H:/R/win-library/3.3"

- "C:/Program Files/R/R-3.3.0/library"

Snapshot written to "H:/git/testProj/testProj/packrat/packrat.lock"

Already up to date.

Error in file(con, "rb") : cannot open the connection

In addition: Warning message:

In file(con, "rb") :

  cannot open file 'H:/git/testProj/testProj/packrat/lib-R/base/DESCRIPTION': No such file or directory

> .libPaths()

[1] "H:/R/win-library/3.3"               "C:/Program Files/R/R-3.3.0/library"

When i try it on `C:/` where i have R installed, i get:

> packrat::init(restart = FALSE)

Initializing packrat project in directory:

- "C:/R_projecten/testProj"

Packrat mode off. Resetting library paths to:

- "H:/R/win-library/3.3"

- "C:/Program Files/R/R-3.3.0/library"

Already up to date.

Initialization complete!

Packrat mode on. Using library in directory:

- "C:/R_projecten/testProj/packrat/lib"

After some research I came to the conclusion that it does not seem to work because it adds a `lib-R` folder with `soft links` to the R base packages.

Is there a 'easy' work around? or is it just a limitation of the method used by the packrat...
I now work from `C:/R_projecten`, which works :)

Might the problem be that packrat should work with UNC paths?

Thanks a lot!
Siete Fr

messages.subject: Separation of core work Packages vs dependencies imported from installed packages
messages.subject_clean: Separation of core work Packages vs dependencies imported from installed packages
messages.body_plain:
Something that I've noticed when using packages with Packrat is that when you load packages into your library, it also installs all the dependencies, which is fine, but makes it hard to differentiate
the core packages for a task, vs the imported dependencies. A good example is devtools, which imports a good amount of packages to use. Have you thought about making the Packrat Library displayed only the packages that you installed,
and maybe creating a sub folder for the dependencies so that while they are still there it does not clutter the packages pane in RStudio?

These are just my thoughts, but I'd love to get others opinions on how, or what this would even look like.

Respectfully,

Peter Gensler

messages.subject: Re: Separation of core work Packages vs dependencies imported from installed packages
messages.subject_clean: Separation of core work Packages vs dependencies imported from installed packages
messages.body_plain:
Hi Peter,

One possibility would be to include a new column in the Packages pane, that denotes where / why a particular package is included in a project, but it would be difficult to get the UI exactly right without confusing users, I think.

Installing into a subfolder is also not that simple, since we want the default R workflows (using install.packages, install_github) to work as-is, and those install packages into the 'active' library path with the default behavior, which most users are accustomed to. We could potentially do something like add a new library path and separate packages according to 'used in this project' vs. 'a dependency of a package', but this would add a lot of overall complexity.

A starting point might just be a packrat function that returns the set of packages used / active in a project directly, and the dependencies of each of those packages.

Best,
Kevin
